A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WEBRL and retain matching methods, experiments, and results. Text extraction and visual inspection cover the equations, tables, figures, and all appendices, including relocated material, without material reading gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original WEBRL training and evaluation results, including WebArena-Lite success rates, component ablations, ORM evaluation, and website trajectories.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and reports additional controlled comparisons, repeated-seed results, replay studies, and prompt experiments.

M1.justification: v1 Section 2.2 manually checks generated instructions after critic filtering. v3 Section 2.1 instead develops feasibility rules through manual inspection and uses GPT-4o to filter tasks automatically. The central policy loss, ORM decision rule, and confidence-filtered replay procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both retain HTML-based web tasks across Reddit, GitLab, CMS, Map, and OSS, with evaluation on 165 WebArena-Lite tasks. Added studies vary training components and prompts within this coverage. The revised ORM training-pool description concerns sampling within the retained WebArena domains.

E2.justification: The main Table 1 and ORM comparator sets remain unchanged. Figure 5 replaces DigiRL with WEBRL without curriculum learning and revises the SFT-based no-KL controls to REINFORCE-based controls. Additional experiments evaluate DigiRL with curriculum learning and an alternative KL-based target. DPO and PPO receive conceptual comparisons, not new benchmark evaluations.

E3.justification: Section 3.7 substantially revises the controls used to isolate KL regularization and curriculum learning. New appendix protocols vary critic replay, generation prompts, and loss objectives; the objective comparison also uses different training-data sources. The ORM recipe changes from augmented WebArena tasks and WEBRL/baseline rollouts to baseline rollouts plus original WebArena-Lite demonstrations, still totaling 12,200 samples. These are reported protocol changes, without establishing that the retained headline experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond redesigning Figure 5, v3 adds studies of squared-log versus KL objectives, critic training with historical data, curriculum learning within both WEBRL and DigiRL, failed trajectories in replay, and three task-generation prompts. These address previously untested or confounded design choices. The earlier error-type, task-length, complexity, perplexity, and beta analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v1 provides no repeated-seed uncertainty reporting. v3 Appendix C first reports four distinct seeds for WEBRL, phase-wise error bars in Figure 13, and cross-method error bars with standard-deviation discussion in Figure 15. This substantially expands uncertainty reporting; the PDFs do not establish an increase from any particular earlier run count.

E6.justification: The headline Table 1 and ORM scores remain unchanged, but Figure 5 replaces the SFT-based no-KL results of 30.3% and 9.7% without replay with REINFORCE-based results of 34.5% and 20.0%. It reports 32.7% for WEBRL without curriculum learning. These involve changed conditions, not same-setting gains. New appendix results include prompt success rates of 42.4%, 40.6%, and 43.6% in Table 7, alongside optimizer, replay, curriculum, and repeated-seed findings.

T1.justification: v3 removes v1 Equation 4's reward-only intermediate identity and reward-shaping argument, directly deriving the advantage identity while retaining the final loss. New Appendix A derives the regression and alternative KL objectives, supplies discounted advantage equations, and adds a policy-improvement argument using replay and approximate value estimation. This is a substantial theoretical expansion, although the new proof leaves normalization and replay-policy dominance insufficiently justified.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contribution: self-evolving curriculum RL combining an ORM, KL-constrained updates, and replay to improve open-model web agents. The headline performance and novelty claims are retained; the additional analyses support existing claims rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: Section 3.7 revises the explanation of KL benefits around a REINFORCE control, removing the earlier comparison with SFT's inability to learn from failed trajectories. Section 3.9 explicitly discusses easier generated tasks and rephrasing as aids to exploration. Appendix C adds interpretations of generation-related variability and prompt robustness. The earlier cross-website performance trade-off remains.

D1.justification: v3 adds Algorithm 1 documenting initialization, failure-set accumulation, replay selection, and iterative updates; an explicit observation/action inventory; and website-specific feasibility-filtering instructions. It also provides two alternative generation prompts and a more explicit ORM data recipe. These substantially expand implementation documentation. The existing hyperparameter tables and code/model/data access link are retained.

R1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds focused positioning against DPO, PPO, and AWR, including a table of algorithmic properties and discussion of web-interaction constraints. Supporting references include Fujimoto and Gu, Haarnoja et al., and PPO; related work also adds Carta, Tan, and Zhao citations. The Ng reward-shaping citation is removed. The overall positioning around open-model web-agent training remains stable.

P1.justification: v3 places curriculum generation before reinforcement learning, subdivides the training appendix, and updates cross-references, localized explanations, authorship, and the publication header. Most introduction, results, and conclusion prose remains closely matched. The revision does not extensively rewrite the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands the visual presentation with optimizer and critic plots, uncertainty and curriculum/replay plots, Algorithm 1, an algorithm-comparison table, and a prompt-results table. Figure 5 has revised curves, legends, and vertical scale. Existing prompts, hyperparameter tables, website curves, and the five qualitative examples are relocated rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses important attribution gaps in v1: the no-KL control retains policy-gradient learning, and curriculum effects are tested within WEBRL and DigiRL. Together with repeated-seed uncertainty reporting and fuller training/filtering documentation, this substantially strengthens the central empirical evidence despite unchanged headline scores. The gains are qualified by an incomplete new policy-improvement proof and an ORM data recipe not fully reconciled with the retained main text; the clearest improvement is empirical rigor and inspectability.
